newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen falling sharply vs yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen falling sharply vs yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to keep falling against the yen during Asian trading time on Monday, as traders are likely to sell further amid expectations that the U.S.-Japan interest rate gap will narrow.
A tumble to 117.00 yen is possible with very few bids expected, while Japanese investors' hedge sales may speed up the dollar's fall, dealers said.
"I don't see bids on the downside. A fall to 117 during Tokyo time is possible," said a trust bank dealer. He added substantial bids were not expected until the dollar neared 115 yen.
Dealers said hedge sales by Japanese investors were expected to continue to weigh on the dollar.

With no fresh factors in early Tokyo trading, the dollar had already slipped below 118 yen, the lowest since late January, as traders, mostly interbank, and Japanese investors rushed to sell further. "At this level, nobody is interested in buying," a city bank dealer said.

On Friday, the dollar plunged against the yen from an Asian session high of 123.72 yen to a U.S. session low of about 119.10 yen, the largest intra day fall in the dollar/yen rate since September 1995.
On Saturday, Japanese officials were busy providing yen-supportive comments, while attending the annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Fukuoka.

Asked if a nearly six-yen rise in the past week was an excessive gain, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) International Finance Bureau, said: "No, it is not overly excessive."

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said he believed the yen's rise indicated that foreign exchange markets were finally digesting a Group of Seven (G7) statement made last month on currency stability.
